item.title: Russell Brand’s Own Words Helped Police Test His Denials
item.description: Investigators reviewed Russell Brand’s books, broadcasts and interviews to check witness accounts and identify inconsistencies in his denials. In November 2026, he was convicted of one rape and three sexual assaults and sentenced to 10 years and six months. He was acquitted of three other charges.

item.title: Brad Sigmon Chose South Carolina’s First Firing Squad Execution
item.description: Brad Sigmon, convicted of murdering his ex-girlfriend’s parents, David and Gladys Larke, was executed on March 7, 2025. At 67, he became South Carolina’s oldest executed prisoner and its first put to death by firing squad, choosing it over lethal injection or electrocution.

item.title: A Missing Button Linked Robert Lee Yates To Murder
item.description: Investigators found a button from Jennifer Joseph’s blouse and blood matching her DNA in a Corvette Robert Lee Yates had owned. The evidence helped expose the Spokane serial killer, who pleaded guilty to 13 murders in 2000 and received a 408-year sentence.

item.title: His Confession Ended The 13-Year Search For Brittanee Drexel
item.description: Brittanee Drexel, 17, vanished during a 2009 spring break trip to Myrtle Beach, South Carolina. In 2022, Raymond Moody confessed and led investigators to her remains. He pleaded guilty to kidnapping, rape and murder and was sentenced to life without parole.

item.title: Amie Harwick Had Sought Protection From Her Future Killer
item.description: Los Angeles therapist Amie Harwick obtained restraining orders against ex-boyfriend Gareth Pursehouse years before he killed her at her home in February 2020. He was convicted of murder and residential burglary in 2023 and sentenced to life without parole.
